title: API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization
excerpt: Attackers can exploit API endpoints that are vulnerable to broken object-level authorization by manipulating the ID of an object that is sent within the request.

title: API2:2023 Broken Authentication
excerpt: Doesn't validate the authenticity of tokens ... Doesn't validate the JWT expiration date ... accept unsigned/weakly signed JWT tokens ({"alg":"none"}).

title: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization
excerpt: The API endpoint exposes properties of an object that are considered sensitive and should not be read by the user (previously named: 'Excessive Data Exposure').

title: A01:2021 Broken Access Control
excerpt: Moving up from the fifth position ... Access control enforces policy such that users cannot act outside of their intended permissions. ... Except for public resources, deny by default.

title: A03:2021 Injection
excerpt: Injection slides down to the third position. ... Preventing injection requires keeping data separate from commands and queries. ... CWE-79: Cross-site Scripting.

title: A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration
excerpt: Moving up from #6 in the previous edition, 90% of applications were tested for some form of misconfiguration, with an average incidence rate of 4.51%.

title: A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components
excerpt: If you do not know the versions of all components you use (both client-side and server-side). This includes components you directly use as well as nested dependencies.

title: A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures
excerpt: Previously known as Broken Authentication, this category slid down from the second position ... User sessions or authentication tokens ... aren't properly invalidated during logout or a period of inactivity.

title: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
excerpt: An application relies upon plugins, libraries, or modules from untrusted sources, repositories, and content delivery networks (CDNs). ... Use digital signatures or similar mechanisms to verify the software or data is from the expected source and has not been altered.

title: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
excerpt: Auditable events, such as logins, failed logins, and high-value transactions, are not logged. ... Without logging and monitoring, breaches cannot be detected.

title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics (§15.5.4 403 Forbidden, §15.5.5 404 Not Found)
excerpt: §15.5.4: An origin server that wishes to "hide" the current existence of a forbidden target resource MAY instead respond with a status code of 404 (Not Found). §15.5.5: The 404 (Not Found) status code indicates that the origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource or is not willing to disclose that one exists.

title: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
excerpt: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command.

title: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
excerpt: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

title: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet
excerpt: The bcrypt password hashing function should only be used for password storage in legacy systems where Argon2 and scrypt are not available. ... use a work factor of 10 or more.

title: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet
excerpt: The HttpOnly cookie attribute instructs web browsers not to allow scripts ... to access the cookies via the DOM document.cookie object. The Secure cookie attribute instructs web browsers to only send the cookie through an encrypted HTTPS connection. The SameSite attribute prevents the browser from sending the cookie on cross-site requests, ... providing CSRF defense.

title: RFC 8446: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3
excerpt: This document specifies version 1.3 of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol. ... TLS allows client/server applications to communicate ... in a way that is designed to prevent eavesdropping, tampering, and message forgery.

title: RFC 7519: JSON Web Token (JWT)
excerpt: JSON Web Token (JWT) is a compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties. ... The "exp" (expiration time) claim identifies the expiration time on or after which the JWT MUST NOT be accepted for processing.

title: RFC 6749: The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework
excerpt: Access tokens are credentials used to access protected resources. ... Refresh tokens are credentials used to obtain access tokens ... used to obtain a new access token when the current access token becomes invalid or expires.

title: RFC 6797: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
excerpt: This specification defines a mechanism enabling web sites to declare themselves accessible only via secure connections. ... The REQUIRED 'max-age' directive specifies the number of seconds during which the UA regards the host as a Known HSTS Host.

title: SLSA Provenance (v1.0)
excerpt: Provenance is an attestation that a particular build platform produced a set of software artifacts through execution of the buildDefinition. ... Verifiable information about software artifacts describing where, when and how something was produced.

title: OWASP CycloneDX Bill of Materials Standard
excerpt: OWASP CycloneDX is a full-stack Bill of Materials (BOM) standard that provides advanced supply chain capabilities for cyber risk reduction. ... a modern standard for the software supply chain.

title: OWASP Core Rule Set (CRS)
excerpt: The OWASP CRS is a set of generic attack detection rules for use with ModSecurity or compatible web application firewalls. The CRS aims to protect web applications from a wide range of attacks, including the OWASP Top Ten.

title: NIST Glossary: Least Privilege (per SP 800-12 Rev. 1)
excerpt: A security principle that a system should restrict the access privileges of users (or processes acting on behalf of users) to the minimum necessary to accomplish assigned tasks.

title: NIST SP 800-63B: Digital Identity Guidelines - Authentication and Lifecycle Management
excerpt: At AAL2, reauthentication of the subscriber SHALL be repeated at least once per 12 hours during an extended usage session ... Reauthentication of the subscriber SHALL be repeated following any period of inactivity lasting 30 minutes or longer. ... The session SHALL be terminated (i.e., logged out) when this time limit is reached.

title: Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool - STRIDE Threat Categories
excerpt: Microsoft uses the STRIDE model, which categorizes different types of threats. Spoofing: Involves illegally accessing and then using another user's authentication information ... Elevation of Privilege: An unprivileged user gains privileged access.

title: NIST SP 800-181 Rev. 1: NICE Workforce Framework for Cybersecurity
excerpt: a fundamental reference for describing and sharing information about cybersecurity work. It expresses that work as Task statements and describes Knowledge and Skill statements.
